Reference: Active site‐based analysis of structural proteins for drug targets in different human Coronaviruses (2021). Chemical Biology & Drug Design. https://doi.org/10.1111/cbdd.14004

Region/Domain: Receptor-binding domain (RBD); S1/S2 cleavage region
Importance: SARS, SARS-related coronaviruses, and HCoV-NL63 use ACE2 for entry into human cells. The shared receptor usage and frequent HCoV-NL63 infection are suggested to provide opportunities for evolution of highly pathogenic variants.
Reference: Comparative Analyses of ACE2 Receptor Binding Corona Viruses that Cause Mild versus Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome in Humans (2021). Microbiology Research Journal International. https://doi.org/10.9734/MRJI/2021/V31I230299

Protein: HCoV-229E Spike (S) protein, SARS-CoV Spike (S) protein, SARS-CoV-2 Spike (S) protein
Region/Domain: S1 C-terminal domain receptor-binding domain (RBD), including receptor-binding motif (RBM)
Binds To: HCoV-229E RBD binds human aminopeptidase N (hAPN); SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 RBDs bind human ACE2 (hACE2)
Importance: The RBD directly binds host receptors and is an important target for neutralizing-antibody induction. SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 RBDs have larger receptor-binding interfaces and standing conformations associated with stronger RBD-specific antibody responses, whereas the lying HCoV-229E RBD induces fewer RBD-targeting neutralizing antibodies.
Reference: Insight into Vaccine Development for Alphacoronaviruses Based on Structural and Immunological Analyses of Spike Proteins (2020). Journal of Virology. https://doi.org/10.1128/JVI.02284-20

Protein: SARS-CoV-2 conserved peptides from NSP1, helicase, nsp14 exonuclease, Spike glycoprotein, and ORF3a
Region/Domain: Conserved B- and T-cell epitopes (8-23 amino acids), including QETSNSSLFC, LHRVEERCLLLP, VYLEDKFDLL, ESATVLLII, TLSLNELLISKLNDNVKRQLYG, HNLLSLCRLQLLCFL, and FLWIKIRVGQSAEFI
Binds To: HLA class I alleles (HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C)
Importance: These conserved SARS-CoV-2 peptides were predicted to bind HLA class I molecules and may elicit cellular immune responses. Many predicted HLA-binding peptides were associated with HLA alleles linked to autoimmune/hyper-inflammatory conditions, other viral infections, and drug-induced illnesses.
Reference: Immunoinformatics prediction of potential immunodominant epitopes from human coronaviruses and association with autoimmunity (2022). Immunogenetics. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00251-021-01250-5

Protein: Seasonal HCoV spike proteins (229E, OC43, HKU1, NL63), SARS-CoV spike protein, SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, SARS-CoV-2 N protein
Region/Domain: SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) and N-terminal domain (NTD)
Binds To: Serum immunoglobulin G antibodies from HCoV-infected participants
Importance: Binding antibodies to seasonal HCoV spike proteins were high, showed little increase after infection, and were maintained over time. Homologous preinfection antibody binding did not significantly correlate with infection odds, and there was little cross-response to SARS-CoV-2 proteins.
Reference: Coronavirus Occurrence in the Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation (HIVE) Cohort of Michigan Households: Reinfection Frequency and Serologic Responses to Seasonal and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronaviruses (2021). The Journal of Infectious Diseases. https://doi.org/10.1093/infdis/jiab161

Region/Domain: Receptor-binding domain (RBD)
Importance: Neutralizing antibodies recognizing the RBD and other spike epitopes can prevent ACE2 receptor binding, membrane fusion, and viral entry. Such antibodies are a basis for vaccines and therapeutic/preventive monoclonal antibodies.
Reference: COVID-19 and the Path to Immunity (2020). JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2020.16656

Region/Domain: NA
Binds To: human ACE2; spike proteins of all human coronaviruses
Importance: Spike protein interaction with ACE2 indicated that immobilized HCoV proteins on the microarray were properly folded and functional. Surfactant protein D showed broad affinities for spike proteins across all human coronaviruses.
Reference: Development and Application of Human Coronavirus Protein Microarray for Specificity Analysis (2021). Analytical Chemistry. https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.1c00614

Region/Domain: NA
Binds To: cellular entry receptors: human aminopeptidase N (APN), angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), and dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4)
Importance: Specific binding of coronavirus spike protein to cellular entry receptors is described as an initial step of coronavirus infection. APN is listed for HCoV-229E, ACE2 for HCoV-NL63, SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2, and DPP4 for MERS-CoV.
Reference: December 2021 Pulmonary Case of the Month: Interstitial Lung Disease with Red Knuckles (2021). Southwest Journal of Pulmonary and Critical Care. https://doi.org/10.13175/swjpcc066-21
Journal: Southwest Journal of Pulmonary and Critical Care

Region/Domain: Catalytic binding site; catalytic residues His41 and Cys145; substrate-binding subsites S1-S5
Binds To: Hypericin, rosmarinic acid, isorhamnetin, and luteolin
Importance: These natural compounds bind the Mpro catalytic site and inhibit enzymatic activity, supporting Mpro as a target for broad-spectrum coronavirus inhibitors. Hypericin and isorhamnetin also bind and inhibit SARS-CoV-1 Mpro, while hypericin binds and inhibits MERS-CoV Mpro.
Reference: In Silico and In Vitro Identification of Pan-Coronaviral Main Protease Inhibitors from a Large Natural Product Library (2022). Pharmaceuticals. https://doi.org/10.3390/ph15030308

Region/Domain: fusion peptide; receptor binding domain (RBD)
Importance: Polyclonal antibody targeting of SARS-CoV-2 spike peptides, including cross-reactive epitopes in the conserved fusion peptide, correlated with convalescent plasma functionality. Plasma preferentially reactive to the SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD rather than the HKU1 RBD had higher neutralizing titers.
Reference: Antibody responses to endemic coronaviruses modulate COVID-19 convalescent plasma functionality. (2021). The Journal of clinical investigation. https://doi.org/10.1172/JCI146927

Region/Domain: C-terminal PDZ-binding motif (PBM)
Importance: The PBMs of SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, and SARS-CoV-2 E proteins were predicted to be more flexible than those of less virulent human coronaviruses. This increased flexibility may enable binding to different host proteins and contribute to more severe disease.
Reference: Comparative studies of the seven human coronavirus envelope proteins using topology prediction and molecular modelling to understand their pathogenicity (2021). bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.03.08.434384

Region/Domain: Receptor-binding domain (RBD)
Importance: The RBD-ACE2 interaction is crucial for SARS-CoV-2 attachment and cellular entry. Compounds 9, 14, and 15 bind the spike RBD and interact with hotspot residues required for RBD-ACE2 binding, inhibiting viral entry.
Reference: Identification of nitrile-containing isoquinoline-related natural product derivatives as coronavirus entry inhibitors in silico and in vitro. (2024). Biomedicine & pharmacotherapy = Biomedecine & pharmacotherapie. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biopha.2024.117517

Region/Domain: N-terminal domain (NTD), RNA-binding pocket; residues including Thr2, Ala3, Ser4, Arg41, Arg45, Tyr62, Tyr64, Gly69, Pro70, Thr101, Arg102, and Ala109
Importance: The NP NTD RNA-binding pocket is a potential antiviral drug target. Compounds 1 and 4 bound this domain in vitro, suggesting they may inhibit NP function in SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Reference: Potential Coronaviral Inhibitors of the Nucleocapsid Protein Identified In Silico and In Vitro from a Large Natural Product Library (2022). Pharmaceuticals. https://doi.org/10.3390/ph15091046

Region/Domain: RBD residues 533-588; fusion peptide (FP) residues 813-868; HR2 region (residues not specified)
Binds To: antibodies in COVID-19 convalescent plasma, including cross-reactive antibodies recognizing homologous endemic human coronavirus Spike peptides
Importance: Antibody reactivity to the Spike RBD region was greater in highly neutralizing plasma. Conserved Spike FP and HR2 epitopes showed cross-reactivity with endemic coronavirus antibodies and may represent pre-existing or boosted responses that influence SARS-CoV-2 plasma functionality and potential heterologous protection.
Reference: Antibody responses to endemic coronaviruses modulate COVID-19 convalescent plasma functionality (2020). medRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.12.16.20248294

Region/Domain: S1 subunit receptor-binding domain (RBD)
Importance: Spike receptor binding is required before the S2 subunit mediates membrane fusion and viral entry into host cells. Spike is also a major target of neutralizing antibodies and SARS-CoV-2 vaccine strategies.
Reference: Coronavirus Pseudotypes for All Circulating Human Coronaviruses for Quantification of Cross-Neutralizing Antibody Responses (2021). Viruses. https://doi.org/10.3390/v13081579

Region/Domain: NA
Importance: The temporal emergence of spike protein variants is best explained by optimization of receptor binding affinity, rather than antigenic drift.
Reference: Human endemic coronavirus emergence in the context of past and recent zoonotic outbreaks (2021). Unknown journal. https://doi.org/10.21203/RS.3.RS-134999/V1

Region/Domain: NA
Importance: The spike protein mediates coronavirus entry into host cells through receptor recognition and membrane fusion.
Reference: Bacteriolysis by Zinc Ions-Induced PGN Autolysins, Virucide by ZAP, ZBD, ZnONPs, and Prevaling Zinc Ions-Mediated HCoVs Matter (2020). Unknown journal. https://doi.org/10.22259/IJRSMHS.0503001
